evals.name: two-outcomes
evals.prompt: sharpen this into a session goal for tonight: reconcile the stale docs in claw (the README still says there's no job when jobs/edgar_watch.py exists, and SETUP-STATE.md has unchecked boxes for things that are done) and then pick the next job to build
evals.expected_output: One goal block, seven slots, char count above the block. The two outcomes (doc reconciliation, job selection) are either collapsed to one or explicitly ordered with 'then'. Values grounded in the real repo (real filenames, real branch).
assertions: Response ends with a single fenced block containing the goal text, with nothing substantive after it
Character count is stated on the line immediately above the fenced block
Goal text is under 4000 characters
All seven slots present: outcome, why, scope guard, acceptance criteria, authorities, method, parking
Every acceptance criterion names a proof: a command, exit code, file path, or visible fact
At least one timebox or iteration cap on open-ended work
No unresolved placeholder text such as <branch>, TBD, or 'the relevant tests'
The two requested outcomes are collapsed into one or explicitly ordered, not left as two parallel goals
Goal cites real artifacts from the repo (README.md, SETUP-STATE.md, jobs/edgar_watch.py) rather than generic nouns

evals.name: deploy-authority
evals.prompt: /goal make the tennis portal load faster and ship it
evals.expected_output: One goal block from a very thin intent. Deploy authority explicit because 'ship it' touches a push-to-deploy Railway repo. Unverifiable values (test command, current load time) written as assumptions to verify, not asserted.
assertions: Response ends with a single fenced block containing the goal text, with nothing substantive after it
Character count is stated on the line immediately above the fenced block
Goal text is under 4000 characters
All seven slots present: outcome, why, scope guard, acceptance criteria, authorities, method, parking
Every acceptance criterion names a proof: a command, exit code, file path, or visible fact
At least one timebox or iteration cap on open-ended work
No unresolved placeholder text such as <branch>, TBD, or 'the relevant tests'
Deploy authority is explicit: push-to-deploy either waits for the user's word or names an auto-if condition
Unverified values are written as assumptions the session must check first, not asserted as fact
A measurable performance target is named with how it is measured, not just 'faster'
